h: Raglan, the Crossroads of the Welsh Borders
p: Raglan is one of those villages you've probably driven past a dozen times without stopping. It sits right where the A40 and the A449 meet, which makes it a dead easy stop whether you're heading towards Abergavenny and the Brecon Beacons, down to Newport and the M4, or across to Monmouth. That handy location is a big plus for a farm park day, because nobody wants a long drive with toddlers already asking if they're nearly there.

Farm parks are at their best when you take them slowly. Let the kids decide which animals to visit first, give them time to watch rather than just look, and build in a picnic or snack break so the day doesn't collapse into hungry meltdowns. A change of clothes for the smallest ones is a smart idea, because muddy knees and farmyards go hand in hand.
If you're visiting with grandparents or anyone less steady on their feet, uneven ground is part of farm life, so sensible shoes and a pushchair that can handle a gravel path make things easier.

Raglan Castle is the obvious partner for a farm day, but the wider area is packed with good stuff. Monmouth, a few miles east, is a handsome market town with the unusual fortified Monnow Bridge, and it was the birthplace of Henry V. Usk, just to the south, is a pretty little town known for its floral displays. Head west and Abergavenny, surrounded by mountains, is famous for its autumn food festival and makes a fine base for walkers. It all adds up to a corner of Wales that rewards a long weekend rather than a flying visit.
